# Load libraries
***

```{r}
library(lifelihood)
library(tidyverse)
```

# Data preparation
***

Load the dataset from a `.csv` file:

```{r}
# input data
df <- datapierrick |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(par = as.factor(par), geno = as.factor(geno), spore = as.factor(spore))

df |> head()
```

Prepare arguments for the `as_lifelihoodData()` function:

```{r}
# name of the columns of the clutchs into a single vector
clutchs <- generate_clutch_vector(28)
```

*Note: If you have a large number of clutches, it is easier to generate this vector programmatically. See the [Generate clutch names](generate-clutch-names.html) vignette.*

# Create the `lifelihoodData` object

`as_lifelihoodData()` creates a `lifelihoodData` object, which is a list containing all the information needed to run the lifelihood program on a given dataset of individual life histories.

This function mainly takes your dataset and column names as inputs.

The `dist` argument is a data frame with one or more columns selected from
`mortality`, `maturity`, and `reproduction`. Each row specifies one model to
fit. Each cell must contain `"wei"` (Weibull), `"exp"` (exponential), `"gam"`
(gamma), or `"lgn"` (log-normal). Include only the events you want to fit. For
example, a mortality-only model can use `dist = data.frame(mortality = "wei")`
and needs only the death interval columns. Fitting reproduction also requires
maturity and death interval data, even when those events are not fitted.

This example fits all three events, so its `dist` includes all three:

```{r}
dataLFH <- as_lifelihoodData(
  df = df,
  sex = "sex",
  sex_start = "sex_start",
  sex_end = "sex_end",
  maturity_start = "mat_start",
  maturity_end = "mat_end",
  clutchs = clutchs,
  death_start = "death_start",
  death_end = "death_end",
  matclutch = FALSE,
  covariates = c("par", "geno"),
  dist = data.frame(mortality = "wei", maturity = "gam", reproduction = "lgn")
)
```

# Get the results
***

## All default parameters

Once you have created your `lifelihoodData` object with `as_lifelihoodData()`, call `lifelihood()` to run the lifelihood program.

This returns a `lifelihoodResults` object, which is a list containing the analysis results.

This is a minimal example that specifies only the `lifelihoodData` object, the configuration, and the seeds (four integers used by the lifelihood program's Mersenne Twister pseudorandom number generator). The `raise_estimation_warning` argument is covered in the [next vignette](customize-parameter-boundaries-and-estimation-warning.html).

```{r}
config <- list(
  mortality = list(expt_death = "par", survival_param2 = 1, ratio_expt_death = 1),
  maturity = list(expt_maturity = 1, maturity_param2 = 1),
  reproduction = list(
    expt_reproduction = 1,
    reproduction_param2 = 1,
    n_offspring = 1
  )
)

results <- lifelihood(
  lifelihoodData = dataLFH,
  config = config,
  seeds = c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  raise_estimation_warning = FALSE
)
summary(results)
```

# Get specific results
***

The `lifelihoodResults` object is a list containing all the results of the analysis. We can get specific results by calling the list element.

```{r}
coef(results)
coeff(results, "expt_death")
coeff(results, "survival_param2")

AIC(results)
BIC(results)

logLik(results)

prediction(results, parameter_name = "expt_death") |> head()
prediction(results, parameter_name = "expt_death", type = "response") |> head()
```

# Fit several models at once
***

To compare distribution families, supply one row per model. For example, the
following fits a Weibull/gamma/log-normal model and an exponential model:

```{r}
data_multiple <- dataLFH
data_multiple$dist <- data.frame(
  mortality = c("wei", "exp"),
  maturity = c("gam", "exp"),
  reproduction = c("lgn", "exp")
)

results_multiple <- lifelihood(
  lifelihoodData = data_multiple,
  config = config,
  n_fit = 2,
  raise_estimation_warning = FALSE
)

comparison <- summary(results_multiple$all_models)
comparison
```

`n_fit` applies to every row of `dist`, so this example runs four fits. Each
replicate receives fresh random seeds. Leave `seeds = NULL` when `n_fit > 1`;
with `n_fit = 1`, explicit seeds are reused for each model.

All models share the configuration. In a batch with multiple rows, second
parameters (`survival_param2`, `maturity_param2`, and `reproduction_param2`) are
automatically set to `"not_fitted"` for exponential events, which have no second
parameter. Other events keep their configured formulas. For a single-model fit,
an exponential event with a fitted second parameter raises a warning and that
parameter is disabled before fitting.

`results_multiple` contains the fit with the highest log-likelihood. The
comparison table includes every model and replicate, sorted by AICc, with the
difference from the lowest AICc in its `ΔAICc` column. The first row of this table
can differ from the model with the highest log-likelihood because AICc accounts
for the number of parameters. Use the `fit` column to retrieve a particular fit:

```{r}
best_aicc <- results_multiple$all_models[[comparison$fit[1]]]
best_aicc$dist
```

Each fit stores only its own row of `dist`; prediction, simulation, and
goodness-of-fit therefore use that model's distributions. Batch fitting also
works with `group_by_group = TRUE`. When default parameter boundaries are used,
they are computed separately for each model. A supplied `param_bounds_df`
applies to every model in the batch.
